division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause. The better houses take the Randolph–Washington tier a block back from the trade, and the north tier under Kinzie: off the noise, on dry ground, with a garden. Inferred — the town holds one documented H roof and it is Cobweb Castle, on the north side, which is itself the clause's own outlier. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

ruled.what_happened: DRAWN UNDER A RULING, NOT A QUOTA. The household model drew this house married at 5, and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell; no woman the town already holds fits him either. T-2021 ruled that such a house is given its whole drawn family while the town stays inside the model's own range for 1 July 1835 — at most 3,265, the November count — and this house was admitted under it. The wife and children are the ones the model drew for this house from its own seeds, at the `reconstructed` tier; no source names them, and none says Charles H Beaubien married.

dated_bounds.note: A BOUND ON PRESENCE, AND NOTHING FURTHER. Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 records a man who presented himself and voted, so the entry places a body in Chicago no later than 1834-08-11. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes: a man on a roll of 1833, 1834 or 1835 is not thereby at Chicago on 1 July 1835. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT. The reading of the roll is documented — the town's own paper, held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository, twice mediated by Schulz's transcription and Genealogy Trails' republication, which this project has not gone behind. What no source states is that the man on the roll is the person on this card: data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json joins them on a name, by its rule “one resident of the surname 'Beaubien' agrees with the entry's forenames; 18 bearer(s) of the surname were considered.”, and forenames agree initial for initial: entry 'Charles H. Beaubien' against resident 'Charles H Beaubien'. A bound whose subject is inferred is an inferred bound. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented once and corroborated by nothing else, so the weakest rung of `inferred` the owner's ladder defines. A SINGLE APPEARANCE AND NOTHING ELSE. Read from poll_1834. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G3), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Beaubien, Charles H.” (poll_1834_009, line 178). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Beaubien' agrees with the entry's forenames; 8 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

merge_ruling.for_merge: One forename, one surname, one window. `beaubien_charles_h` stands on the 1833-1835 voter lists and Fergus 1839 prints him a VIOLINIST; `beaubien_charles` stands on the St Mary's baptismal register of 1833-1835. A middle initial present on one printing and absent on the other is the commonest shape in this file, and nothing the two cards carry contradicts the other.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE BEAUBIENS ARE THE ONE FAMILY IN THIS TOWN WHERE A SHARED FORENAME PROVES NOTHING. The layer already holds Jean Baptiste and Mark, and the family is large, French-speaking and heavily represented in exactly the two sources these two cards stand on — a parish register and a voter list. Neither card is an ANCHOR in C3's sense: one is a roll, the other a register entry, and the violinist trade is an 1839 reading that says nothing about which Charles stood at the font in 1834. C4 cannot fire because no middle initial is contradicted, only absent, and R4's want of a second discriminator is precisely the gap here. This wants the page and not a rule.

AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a poll, tax or muster list names a person 20 or over - the 1840 schedule's own adult line. THE FRANCHISE'S AGE RULE IS NOT IN ANY SOURCE RECORD THIS PROJECT HOLDS; this is the model's conditioning and not a reading (T-1303's finding, handed to T-1304). No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. beaubien_charles_h, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e0081 (contested, so nothing crossed).
